subject.title: CLI deadline re-runs an already-accepted prompt on a gateway-fallback session (duplicate-write hazard)

question: For an accepted Gateway run that exceeds `openclaw agent`'s CLI deadline, should the CLI return an attachable in-flight result by default and prohibit embedded rerun, while retaining embedded fallback only for pre-acceptance transport failures?
rationale: The current fallback is documented as an intentional availability behavior, but it conflicts with exactly-once execution and configured agent/provider policy for mutating work; selecting the default recovery contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: No rerun after acceptance
options.body: Return an in-flight timeout with the accepted run and session identifiers, and use embedded fallback only when the Gateway never accepted the request.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in fallback
options.body: Keep an opt-in CLI mode for a new embedded run after deadline expiry, with conspicuous output that it is a separate execution and may use different runtime routing.

options.title: Preserve current default
options.body: Keep automatic timeout fallback and document that users must choose a timeout larger than any non-idempotent task.

recommendation.title: No rerun after acceptance
recommendation.body: Return an in-flight timeout with the accepted run and session identifiers, and use embedded fallback only when the Gateway never accepted the request.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the available history signal for the existing `gateway-fallback-*` timeout-isolation behavior.
